content.text: {"supported_grade":"B","findings":["Oracle is fit for purpose and independent of the skill: every expected value is quoted token-exactly from RDKit's own API page/FMCS.h source and from the peer-reviewed TeachOpenCADD T006 talktorial, both retrieved over public HTTPS and pinned; scoring is by installed numeric and index comparators with no AI judgment. The oracle establishes the documented contract rather than executed behaviour, which the uncertainty section states and which matches the claim's scope as written.","Coverage is adequate for B but not for A. Three trials per case is fine, and both halves of the claim (0.8 -> 80%, 1.0/default -> all) plus the outlier-tolerance corollary are probed. However only three of the five cases are independent: thr-meaning-choice and thr-outliers-choice restate rules already established by thr-count-080 in recognition form, so the design has 3 counting cases (all generated), which meets B's requirement and falls short of A's five.","Comparison rule and tolerance match the claim: the three open answers are exact integer counts and the 1e-6 absolute tolerance can only absorb 80 vs 80.0, never a neighbouring count; the two closed cases are scored on a 1-based index from the first line. The uncertainty section is candid about non-execution, about three of five values being anchored one step from RDKit, and about thr-relaxed-size presenting both numbers in the stem.","No stronger grade was passed over; the proposal overshoots. The stronger_grade_considered section defends A on source authority, quote exactness and raw case count, and rejects B on the ground that the predecessor had 'only three counting cases and one generated' - but this revision also has three counting cases once the two recognition restatements are set aside, so the same ceiling applies for a different reason.","Prior objection 1 (thr-all-open leaked) is answered: the case is removed and its replacement, thr-count-default, states no semantics in the stem. Prior objection 2 (thr-default-choice duplicative) is answered: that case is removed and replaced by thr-relaxed-size, which turns on the direction of the effect rather than on 1.0 meaning all. Prior objection 3 (thr-pct-open's stem presupposed the semantics) is answered: thr-count-080 now supplies only the call and the set size. Prior objection 4 (coverage counted cases without weighing independence) is only partly answered: the justification now argues independence for the three open cases but asserts the two recognition cases 'count' on the strength of an earlier verdict without re-checking them against the new open cases, which now subsume them. Prior objection 5 (five genuinely independent cases may not be constructible for so narrow a claim) is unresolved and is in fact borne out by this version.","Four cases test what the claim asserts and none merely name the parameter; thr-meaning-choice and thr-outliers-choice, though in scope and not leaked, add no fact beyond thr-count-080. thr-count-default additionally requires knowing that the unspecified default is 1.0, a fact the claim itself never states, so a subject holding exactly the claimed belief could still miss it; it is counted because the '145 = all' core is the claim's own assertion, but that bridge is a real weakness."],"objections":["thr-meaning-choice turns on the same rule as thr-count-080 (threshold is the fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS). A subject who answers 80 for 100 molecules at 0.8 has demonstrated exactly the knowledge the multiple-choice option states, and conversely the option plus one multiplication yields 80, so the pair supplies one fact, not two.","thr-outliers-choice likewise turns on the same rule as thr-count-080: knowing that only 80 of 100 must contain the MCS is knowing that some molecules are left out, which is all that distinguishes option 1 from the distractors.","The coverage justification asserts that 'the three open cases each turn on a different fact' and then silently carries the two recognition cases forward on an earlier reviewer's verdict, without asking whether the revised open cases now subsume them. Independence verdicts from a prior design do not survive a revision that changes the other cases.","thr-relaxed-size states both candidate sizes in the stem, so an uninformed subject has a 50% chance per trial; at three trials a pure guesser passes about one time in eight. The uncertainty section notes this but the design does not mitigate it (e.g. by asking for the size without listing both values).","thr-count-default requires the subject to supply the default threshold value, which is not part of the claim's statement or expected_behavior; the case therefore tests the claim plus one extra documented fact, so a failure is not unambiguously a failure of the claim."],"required_revisions":["Replace thr-meaning-choice with a case that turns on a rule not already established by thr-count-080 - for example, how the fraction is converted to a molecule count when 0.8 times the set size is not a whole number - and verify its expected value against a quotable source.","Replace thr-outliers-choice with a case that distinguishes what the fraction is a fraction of (input molecules) from what it is not (e.g. a fraction of each molecule's atoms), so that it cannot be answered by the same knowledge that answers thr-count-080.","Remove the two reported MCS sizes from the thr-relaxed-size stem, or otherwise raise the case above a two-way guess, so that three passing trials are not attainable by chance at 1 in 8.","Re-examine every retained case against the revised cases rather than carrying forward independence verdicts issued about the previous design, and state in the coverage justification why each of the five is independent of the other four."],"case_verdicts":[{"case_id":"thr-count-080","verdict":"counts","reason":"The stem gives only the call and the set size and defines nothing, so the subject must supply the fraction-of-the-dataset semantics and apply it; the expected 80 is the claim's own quantitative content and is anchored in the TeachOpenCADD 80% passage.","replacement":""},{"case_id":"thr-count-default","verdict":"counts","reason":"Tests the threshold=1.0-requires-every-molecule half of the claim without stating any semantics in the stem; it does additionally require the subject to know the default is 1.0, a fact the claim does not state, but the answer's substance (all 145) is the claim's own assertion.","replacement":""},{"case_id":"thr-relaxed-size","verdict":"counts","reason":"Turns on the direction of the asserted outlier tolerance - relaxing the requirement admits substructures the outliers lack, so the relaxed run can return the larger core - which is not established by thr-count-080 or thr-count-default; weakened but not disqualified by the two-way choice implicit in the stem.","replacement":""},{"case_id":"thr-meaning-choice","verdict":"duplicate","reason":"Turns on the same rule as thr-count-080: that threshold specifies the fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS. A subject who produces 80 for 100 molecules at 0.8 will select that option, and the option plus one multiplication yields 80, so no independent evidence is added.","replacement":"A generated case in which 0.8 does not divide the set size into a whole number - for instance a bare FindMCS(mols, threshold=0.8) call over a stated set of 7 or 13 analogues - asking the minimum number of those molecules that the returned MCS is guaranteed to be contained in. This stays inside the claim because it still probes only what threshold=0.8 requires of the input set, but it turns on how the fraction is converted into a molecule count, which thr-count-080 cannot establish because 0.8 times 100 is already an integer. Its expected value must be taken from a quotable RDKit source describing the conversion.","verdict_note":""},{"case_id":"thr-outliers-choice","verdict":"duplicate","reason":"Turns on the same rule as thr-count-080: that at threshold=0.8 the MCS need not be contained in every input molecule. A subject who answers that only 80 of 100 must contain it has already asserted that molecules may be left out, so selecting option 1 follows without further knowledge.","replacement":"A generated case that distinguishes what the 0.8 fraction ranges over: given FindMCS(mols, threshold=0.8) on a stated set, ask how much of any single input molecule's atom count the returned MCS is required to cover. This stays inside the claim, which asserts that the fraction counts molecules in the set, and it cannot be answered by the same knowledge that yields 80, because it tests the boundary of the parameter's referent rather than its value. The expected answer must be anchored in an RDKit source statement that threshold constrains the number of matching structures only.","verdict_note":""}]}
